exposure: early BP screen (6-12 months after delivery)
late BP screen (>=12 months after delivery)
outcome: detection of incident diabetes mellitus type 2
cohort: The study included 4194 women with Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy (HDP) but without pre-existing hypertension, who had at least 6 months of clinical follow-up.
finding: Early postpartum blood pressure screening, performed in a minority of women with HDP, was associated with a significantly higher rate of incident cardiovascular risk factor detection compared to late screening.
